newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman's National Sugar Refinery to float this month.
newsitem.headline: Oman's National Sugar Refinery to float this month.

text.p: Oman's first sugar refinery will open for public subscription this month, one of its founders said on Sunday.
"The shares are being offered to the public this month from about August 15," said sugar trader Ali Redha Darwish, one of eight businessmen setting up the National Sugar Refinery.

Speaking by telephone from Muscat, Darwish put the company's authorised share capital at 15.36 million rials ($40.7 million). Forty percent would be floated, while 60 percent of the funds had been committed by the founders.
Darwish said Gulf Investment Services were managing the flotation.

Work has started to flatten a granite hill within the Mina Qaboos port to make space to build the 360,000-tonne annual capacity plant. Darwish said the refinery would cost about $70 million and take about two years to complete.
The refinery will be the third in the Gulf Arab region, which has one of the highest per capita sugar consumption levels in the world at around 30 kg (66 lb).
